_readme: Every playable character. Edit this file, then run Prince's Palace > Build Default Content. id, displayName and role are required; id is written into save files, so never rename one after a save exists. role names a PrincesPalace.Domain.Content.CharacterRole and attackType a DamageType (both case-insensitive) — CharacterEntryResolver rejects an unknown name at build time rather than shipping a character that silently falls through to the wrong Skill case. THE SIX ABILITY SCORES MUST TOTAL EXACTLY 60. That is a budget, not a floor: differentiation is redistribution, not growth, so a new character cannot be quietly stronger than the roster by being above average at everything — to be tough it has to be feeble somewhere else. A flat 10 across the board already satisfies it, which is what lets exactly one character be designed at a time without touching the others. STAT SPREADS EXPRESS THE ROLE, so a squad's strengths are readable from its species alone, and attackType gives each character an elemental identity for the weakness/resistance system: five characters cover five of the six DamageType values, chosen by loose theme (wool/pasture, sting, bite, cold-blooded shell, old and wise) rather than min-maxed against the enemy roster. TWO ART PATHS, TWO CONVENTIONS, not interchangeable: portraitPath is ASSETS-relative (a head-and-shoulders portrait baked into the scene at build time) while battleSpritePath is RESOURCES-relative with no extension (the full-body stance folder loaded at runtime, produced by tools/slice_actor_sheet.py). Swapping them fails silently — the loader just returns null — so the resolver checks each against its own convention. Both are optional and degrade gracefully: a blank portrait slot, and a plain plate on the fight stage. SIGNATURE RESOURCES are each character's own private combat resource. An EMPTY signatureId means the character has none — that is the meaningful distinction, not a zero capacity (see CombatantState.Signature). All five ride the same three triggers, so a new one is content and wiring rather than a parallel system; what makes them feel different is WHICH trigger dominates. Wool (Shawn) is the balanced template: attack-led with a real per-turn and damage-taken floor, and it is armour and ammunition out of one pool — incoming damage eats it before his health and his abilities shear it off, so every turn is bank-or-spend and both answers are real. His plain Attack pays the most because his Attack is 5 against enemy Defense of up to 9, i.e. nearly worthless as damage; giving it the best Wool yield turns his weakest action into a deliberate choice. He starts every fight at zero, which is why he has the worst opening turn in the game and the best closing one. Venom (Fly) is attack-led and nothing else: fast and fragile, so rewarding getting hit would be a trap for a character who should not be tanking. Fangs (Dog) is per-turn and damage-taken roughly even — a patient hunter also provoked by pain, matching a CrowdControl kit that wants to be in the fight a while. Shell (Turtle) is damage-taken-led by a wide margin on the highest capacity of the five: the literal tank converts punishment into its own resource. Insight (Owl) is per-turn-led and almost nothing else: a passive scholarly resource that fills by being present, fitting a backline Support who is often neither attacking nor being hit. SHAWN'S SPREAD is the only authored one so far — physically feeble and dim but tough and patient (STR 7, INT 6 paying for CON 16, WIS 14), with baseStats rebased alongside it (attack 5 -> 7) so the derivation LANDS him where he already was rather than quietly nerfing him: effective Attack stays 5 and Defense stays 4 while HP goes 24 -> 32 and mana 30 -> 38. Speed genuinely drops 10 -> 8, and that is the one deliberate nerf — now that Speed drives how often a combatant acts, 'slowest to get going' is the front half of his identity, and the Sure Hooves talent exists for players who would rather not have it. ROSTER ORDER IS FILE ORDER: sortOrder is assigned from position here, because Resources.LoadAll returns filename order and that silently reshuffles which characters land in the default squad (CLAUDE.md gotcha 4). Turtle is the fourth slot and the first to actually need extra_recruit_slot for a full squad to reach it (base squad size is 3, see SaveData.EffectiveMaxSquadSize); Owl is the fifth and completes the five CharacterRole values.
